human.problem: Card 3 names Jeremiah as the "you" of verse 11 ("deliver Jeremiah"). In verses 13 and 14, the "you" is given over to plunder "for all your sins" and enslaved in a strange land, but cards 7 to 9 leave that "you" open and never mark a shift. Coming right after card 3, the baker will likely think Jeremiah himself is being plundered and enslaved for his sins. The text does not mark who the "you" is in verses 13 and 14.
human.question: When a speech changes who "you" is without saying so, and leaving it open will likely lead the baker to the wrong person, should Papa Dorin say plainly that the text doesn't say who "you" is here? Or should card 3 also leave the "you" of verse 11 open?
